meta.title: Woke: A Guide to Social Justice
meta.author: Titania McGrath
meta.publisher: Constable, an imprint of Little, Brown Book Group

sentences: **Titania McGrath** introduces herself as a rad ical **intersectionalist poet** with a gift for **social justice**.
She claims her **wokeness** is innate, comparing herself to **Joan of Arc**.
Titania shares stories of **performing slam poetry** and **armed peaceful protests**, expressing disdain for **patriarchal constructs** in academia.
She presents herself as a **guiding force** for those struggling to keep up with **modern social justice concepts**, aiming to **mold them** into more "woke" individuals.
Her writing style is **satirical**, bold, and touches on themes of **identity, feminism**, and **privilege**.
In **early 2018**, I was inspired by online activists to become more active on social media to spread awareness about social justice.
The **internet**, the new weapon of choice, is where modern-day "**keyboard warriors**" make a greater impact than historical figures like Martin Luther King.
My newfound activism led to gaining thousands of followers, whom I prefer to call **disciples**.
However, being a woman online exposed me to abuse and criticism, especially regarding my **poetry**.
I've been accused of being shrill and humorless, highlighting the **underlying sexism** and resistance to ideas that don't conform to the status quo.
The author discusses their frustrations with **gender inequality** and **internalized misogyny**.
They highlight the need for women to make empowering career choices to **redress imbalances**.
The text criticizes **Donald Trump's** election victory, attributing it to women who have **internalized misogyny**.
They quote **Linda Sarsour** wishing to "take away" vaginas from women like **Brigitte Gabriel** who disagree with feminist views.
The author encourages ignoring both men and women who oppose feminism as either **misogynists** or have **internalized misogyny**.

Criticism is directed at three influential women – **Christina Hoff Sommers**, **Camille Paglia**, and **Ella Whelan**, whom the author labels as dangerous figures not deserving a platform for their opposition to modern feminist ideals.
Each woman provides a quote critiquing **trigger warnings**, **safe spaces**, and the view of women as weak.
These quotes reflect their disapproval of current **feminist movements** for being **infantilizing** and weak.
The author dismissively calls them **hateful bitches** for questioning feminist doctrines.
In this segment, **intersectional feminism** and **Islam** are explored.
The author emphasizes the importance of treating Muslims with care, especially due to increased stereotypes and biases.
They argue that Muslims are often unjustly scapegoated since **9/11**, and highlight the misconception that Islam and **feminism** are incompatible.

The piece criticizes the reluctance to accept expressions of Islamic culture like the **veil**, and emphasizes how the West needs to address its own cultural failings, like the refusal of a Belfast bakery to support gay marriage, before judging Islam.
The author suggests that Islamophobic opposition to **hijabs** and **burkas** is unfounded.
Despite terrorist acts, the author believes focusing on medieval **Christian** wrongdoings, like the Crusades, is more appropriate than highlighting modern Islamic extremism.
Criticisms of Islam often stem from ignorance of the **intersectionality** theory and the societal backlash following **jihadist terrorism**.
Finally, some right-wing groups claim that Islamic countries mistreat women and LGBTQIA+ people, but the author insists these are progressive misunderstandings of Islamic society.

parts.title: The End of Poetry and Rise of Wokeness

sentences: This book concludes that poetry and art have reached their zenith with **Titania McGrath**.
Despite being frequently admired, they feel the weight of **being misunderstood**, particularly by **men**.
They see their work as a tool for **social justice**, **minority defense**, and **patriarchy dismantling** rather than an ego-driven pursuit.
McGrath calls for compulsory **Gender Studies** in schools to tackle patriarchal norms, advocating for **wokeness** over criticism like being labeled **‘Orwellian’**.
The objective is to eliminate all forms of **bias** and achieve a **woke utopia**.
